shared_qualifications: C1: conditional room-temperature saturated-KCl SCE comparisons. ALS/BAS lists +0.244 V versus SHE for saturated-KCl calomel and discusses 25°C reference operation (https://www.als-japan.com/2137.html); Corrtest lists +0.241 V versus NHE at25°C (https://www.corrtestinstruments.com/en/02437.html). C1a subtracts244 mV; C1b subtracts241 mV. Both are shown as alternative published comparison conventions, not paper uncertainty or constants fitted to CRA. Paper/CRA do not establish the physical calomel reference temperature/calibration. Numerical agreement is conditional on these25°C conventions; test-solution temperature is not assumed to be reference-electrode temperature. Identity uses alloy and test context independently.

PDF p.2 Table1 gives three distinct Cr/Ni/Re analyses. CRA Nos.212/215/218/221 and213/216/219/222 set Re=0.0 despite paper .84/1.84 wt% Re; corresponding CRA Fe balances omit Re as well. Unique Cr/Ni pairs and electrolyte/temperature series identify counterparts independently. These composition errors are preserved, not repaired.

PDF p.2 procedure: initial15 min at least noble passive potential, then50 mV steps every5 min, followed by12–15 h single-potential steady-state runs. Endpoint is least noble potential with non-increasing current and no visible pits. CRA .16666 mV/s equals50/(5×60) as an average step rate; it is not a continuous sweep or the final long-duration protocol.

Source reports general reproducibility ±10–15 mV, not point-specific uncertainties. Registered Fig.2 readings are approximate; the visible0°C markers appear roughly5 mV below some registered values. Original registry readings remain unchanged. No numerical pH is supplied; CRA7.0 is unverified.
